subject: Aurora: Isolation attestation and topology summary
body:
From: Lena Torres <security@auroracorp.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Cc: aurora-security-team@auroracorp.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora request: isolation attestation + annotated topology

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is capturing evidence for an upcoming vendor review (SOC 2 scoped) and we have a couple of asks specific to Dedicated/Private deployments: a compact attestation letter that summarizes the isolation model, an annotated topology PDF, and a brief mapping to SIG/C-AIQ controls related to network segregation.

Can you provide a single package (PDF + CSV mapping) we can attach to the review? Ideal timeline is early next week. Also please include the control-plane demarcation and any optional air-gap patterns for higher-regulated tenants.

Thanks,
Lena Torres
Senior InfoSec Manager
Aurora Corporation

---
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Torres <security@auroracorp.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora request: isolation attestation + annotated topology

Hi Lena — appreciate the clear ask.

We can assemble the package you described. Quick clarification items before we compile:
1) Is the SOC 2 scope limited to the hosted Redwood Dedicated pools (Redwood Dedicated) or do you also need Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployment examples for each control?
2) For annotated topology, do you want a high-level single-page diagram or per-region/export-ready diagrams (we can include both).
3) Do you have a template for the attestation letter, or should we use our standard cover (serial-numbered) attestation?

Plan: I will pull the isolation matrix and a topology PDF and ask Kimberly and Karthik to add the SIG/CAIQ mapping. We should be able to deliver a draft by COB Jul 14 PT and a signed attestation by Jul 15 if that timeline works.

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(Attachment placeholders: aurora_vpc_topology_v3.pdf — topology diagram, redwood_isolation_matrix.csv — control mapping, attestation_cover_letter.pdf — attestation cover)

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora request: isolation attestation + annotated topology

Vanessa / team — draft notes for the package below. I focused on the security control mapping and included operational constraints that auditors typically look for.

Attachment: redwood_isolation_matrix.csv (row excerpts shown inline)
- Control: Network Segmentation (SIG v2.1: NET-01 / CAIQ Network Segmentation) — Claim: Tenant traffic is logically separated using per-tenant virtual routing + per-pool security groups; Dedicated pools run in customer-dedicated GPU hosts with hypervisor/host isolation. Evidence: topology diagram page 1 + VPC ACL snippets (redacted).
- Control: Control Plane Separation (SIG: CNTL-02) — Claim: Control plane services run in a separate management VPC with one-way egress to telemetry collectors; no customer compute can initiate control-plane config changes. Evidence: diagram annotations, excerpt from RBAC config change log.
- Control: Egress & Data Exfil Protection (CAIQ: Data Leakage controls) — Claim: Egress is funneled through egress proxies with DLP policies and per-customer allowlists. Evidence: egress proxy config, sample DLP rule set.

Optional patterns to include (per Lena's ask):
- Air-gapped private deploy (on‑prem): isolated management plane delivered via a physically segregated cluster, optional HSM-backed KMS.
- Sidecar-proxy tenancy model: per-tenant sidecars for network filtering and observability when customers require finer-grained controls.

I will produce a short narrative paragraph for each claim for the attestation cover letter and point to the specific artifacts. Karthik — can you add the kernel/VM footprint statement for Dedicated GPU hosts (quick blurb on hypervisor patch cadence and image hardening)?

Kimberly Park
Head of Security Architecture
Redwood Inference

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora request: isolation attestation + annotated topology

Quick add:
- Dedicated hosts use a minimal host image with a hardened kernel; we run automated image builds with signed artifacts. Patch cadence: host OS patch baseline validated weekly, critical CVEs triaged to a 72‑hour remediation SLA for Dedicated.
- KV cache and model artifacts: model weights and KV cache are stored on ephemeral volumes mounted on GPU nodes; persistent customer data is only stored in encrypted object storage with per-tenant prefixes. Keys are managed via customer-specific KMS keys for Private deployments and by Redwood KMS for Hosted when customers don't bring their own.
- Telemetry path: control-plane telemetry is write-only for customer compute; we include attestations in the topology PDF pointing to the telemetry collector endpoints.

I will prepare a 1‑page technical appendix to accompany the topology and the CSV mapping.

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Manager, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

Hi Vanessa — thanks, that timeline works. Two quick clarifications from our side: 1) for the air-gap/on‑prem pattern can you explicitly state whether the management control plane requires an outbound connection for licensing/updates (some of our auditors flag any outbound as an issue); 2) can you include a short blurb about key rotation policy for customer-managed KMS?

If you can include those items in the attestation that should be enough for initial review.

— Pete
Principal Engineer, Aurora Corp

---
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Pete Hughes <pete.hughes@auroracorp.com>, Lena Torres <security@auroracorp.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora request: isolation attestation + annotated topology

Pete / Lena — delivering the draft package attached. Summary of the two points you flagged:

1) Management control-plane egress for on‑prem/air‑gapped deploys: Optional. For fully air-gapped installs we provide an offline update bundle model — no persistent outbound connection is required. If customers choose the management-plane telemetry option, we use an allow-listed outbound connection to our update/telemetry endpoints over TLS with mutual auth. We will note both options in the attestation.

2) Customer-managed KMS key rotation: For BYOK scenarios, customers retain key ownership and rotate per their own policy; Redwood supports automated rotation hooks and can rotate wrapped data keys on a customer schedule with rotation metadata recorded in the audit log. For Redwood-managed keys, rotation follows a 90‑day rotation cycle for data‑keys and we publish rotation events to the customer audit feed.

Attachments (attached): aurora_vpc_topology_v3.pdf, redwood_isolation_matrix.csv, attestation_cover_letter.pdf
Download link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Auroa-Redwood-Attestation
HubSpot record: HS-12345

Let me know if you want any small edits before I sign the attestation cover letter.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
